newsitem.title: USA: One cadet leaves Citadel over alleged hazing. [CORRECTED 19:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: One cadet leaves Citadel over alleged hazing. [CORRECTED 19:50 GMT]

text.p: The Citadel said Monday that one cadet had been dismissed from the military-style college in connection with hazing allegations made by two of its first female cadets. (Corrects to show cadet was dismissed and did not resign.)

Major-General Clifton Poole, interim president of the school, also told a news conference that nine other cadets implicated in the alleged hazing were being punished and that charges against one cadet were dismissed for lack of evidence. Boards appointed by the Citadel's Commandant held hearings earlier this month into the alleged involvement of 11 cadets in hazing of Jeanie Mentavlos and Kim Messer, who quit the school in January.
School officials said the punishments for the nine cadets included being ordered to march round the campus and "sitting confinement" -- being required to sit down for prescribed periods of time.

Mentavlos and Messer, who were among four women enrolled at the state-funded school after it changed its all-male admissions policy last summer, had complained of physical abuse and sexual harassment.
Four other male cadets alleged to have been involved in the hazing were disciplined in December. Three resigned -- one by not returning to campus for a second semester -- and one was punished.
